task: round 13 scan_hyp_node_count (node-count lever on K2; per-embryo; public-density break-even)
summary: NODE-COUNT LEVER, measured on the exp60 ins35 bed (K2-like; parity ALL 0.93988; 56 clips; official metric; scratchpad r13nc/). Metric arithmetic: J_adj = J*(1 - 0.1*(N_pred - N_est)/N_est) with no clip at 1. Dropping 1% of nodes at zero TP cost is worth +0.00090 pooled (44b6 +0.00063, because N_pred/N_est = 0.71 there; 6bba +0.00093, N_pred/N_est = 1.02). Dropping a uniform random 1% costs -0.018 to -0.021, about 21x the bonus, because each matched node carries 1.85 TP edges. The measured break-even enrichment is r* = (group match rate) / (embryo base rate) ~ 0.047 pooled (44b6 0.029, 6bba 0.049). Enrichment is about the same in both embryos (readmit 0.17/0.16, components <= 8 nodes 0.22/0.21, synthetic 0.40/0.32), so the public embryo's annotation density does NOT decide the sign; it only sets the noise. Round 11's 'P(annotated) < ~0.2%' is r* times the pooled base rate; per embryo that is ~0.02-0.04% on 44b6 and ~0.25% on 6bba. Under the other model, where a group's absolute match rate is fixed, generic pruning would need a public density above ~12-15% (readmit, short components), which is impossible. Every generic low-evidence group is at r = 0.13-0.44, 3-9x above r*: random -0.019, readmit +0.0005 (44b6 -0.0023), synthetic -0.0027, node max-p < 0.3 -0.0013, MIN_TRACK_LEN 7 / 9 equivalents -0.0003 / -0.0003. The only positive groups are end-leaves on a weak edge and low-p components. They win half through the node factor and half by deleting FP edges into annotated tracks. Exact K2-builder lp30 (applied before the insertion): +0.00096 [+0.00057, +0.00139], W/L 52/4, 44b6 +0.0014, 0.51% of nodes. The forum claim 'LB tracks node count' is asymmetric in our records. Added nodes cost the full node factor (probe 11: +3.2% nodes -> -0.003; probe 6 -0.002). Generic removal does not pay (probe 9 -0.001; det 0.99 -0.005). Leaf prune tied twice (P27, P36 display 0; P36 unrounded above #35). The ONLY existing-knob pruning rung is exp70a = K2 + LEAF_PRUNE_MIN_EDGE_PROB 0.3, and it is already submitted (probe 40, PENDING, expected ~04:30-05:00Z). Its expected public move is ~+0.0002 (1/6 rule) up to ~+0.0005 (node-term half at full transfer). That can flip the display only if K2's unrounded score sits within ~0.0002-0.0005 of 0.9545; P ~0.1-0.25. No other existing knob prunes profitably, and lp50 is a lab-equal threshold neighbour (I-310). New prunes need new code: a track-START mirror of lp30 (+0.00048 lab, 44b6 17/0) and low-mean-p components (+0.00061, with a -0.013 cliff at threshold 0.7). Each is worth ~+0.0001 public, below the R8 bar, so both go on the post-deadline list. Nothing new reaches R8. Finals and L9 are unchanged.

findings.what: Node-factor arithmetic, measured on the K2-like lab. Free-drop value per 1% of nodes: +0.00090 pooled, 44b6 +0.00063, 6bba +0.00093. N_pred/N_est: pooled 0.88, 44b6 0.71, 6bba 1.02. Weighted J 0.919. Random 1% drop, 3 seeds: -0.0211 / -0.0175 / -0.0184, 1.85 TP edges lost per matched node. Measured break-even enrichment r* = free-drop value / random-drop cost = 0.047 pooled (44b6 0.029, 6bba 0.049). The analytic form is r* = 0.1*ebar*R*rho/(f*e), with ebar ~0.94 GT edges per matched node, R edge recall, rho = N_pred/N_est, and e TP edges per dropped matched node (~2 interior, ~1 leaf). This gives ~0.045*rho for interior nodes and ~0.09*rho for leaves; the embryo density cancels.

findings.what: Answer to 'what annotation density on the PUBLIC embryo would make pruning pay': none. Enrichment is embryo-invariant: readmit r 0.17 (44b6) / 0.16 (6bba); components <= 8 nodes 0.22 / 0.21; random ~1.0 / 1.0; synthetic 0.40 / 0.32. The absolute match rate scales with density, readmit 0.13% vs 0.83% (model A). The sign therefore depends on r vs r*, not on density. Density only sets the noise: 44b6 CIs are 3-5x wider, because 17 clips hold 3,192 matched nodes against 37,601 on 6bba. Under the alternative model B (fixed absolute match rate q), pruning pays only when d > q/r*. That means d > ~14% for short components (q 0.67%) and d > ~12% for readmit (q 0.55%), far above both train embryos (0.79%, 5.20%). Round 11's 'pays only if P(annotated) < ~0.2%' is model A at the pooled base rate. It is correct as an order of magnitude, but the absolute threshold is embryo-specific: ~0.02-0.04% on 44b6 and ~0.25% on 6bba. The readmit sign flip by embryo (44b6 -0.0023, 6bba +0.0008) is not a density effect. It is FP-edge removal (6bba dFP -44, 44b6 +4) plus small-sample noise (7 TP on 44b6 = -0.0018).

findings.what: START-LEAF PRUNE (mirror of lp30 on track starts): drop a node with in-degree 0 and exactly one outgoing edge, not on the first frame, whose edge has p < 0.3 (edges without p exempt). Lab on the ins35 bed: +0.00048 [+0.00018, +0.00083], 44b6 +0.00052 (17/0, 0 matched), 6bba +0.00048, W/L 51/5, 0.36% of nodes. The threshold is lp30's own, not tuned. Stacked with lp30 it is roughly additive, ~+0.0014 lab (not measured jointly). Expected public ~+0.0001 (1/6 rule). Runtime ~0 (one pass over the edges per clip, <1 s on ~100 clips). Needs a NEW builder patch (a startprune copy of prune_weak_leaf_nodes), tests, the byte-identical-when-off check, a dummy and a NEW user OK by 27 Sep 12:00Z (R8). Lab EV is ~25x below the +0.012 bar, and as a public rung it would be a node-count knob climb of the kind P27 / P36 already read as 0.
